REFERENCE

Reading the atlas

The catalog uses the NASA Exoplanet Archive’s Planetary Systems Composite Parameters table. Systems without a cataloged distance and sky position appear in search and system details. Sol provides a map reference.

Water vapor
Selected atmospheric detections with a source on each planet. Coverage is partial.
Rocky candidate
Catalog radius up to 1.6 Earth radii, with bulk density at least 3.5 g/cm³ when available. Composition remains uncertain. See Rogers (2015) for the radius threshold.
Cold / possibly frozen
Catalog equilibrium temperature at or below 200 K. Surface conditions and ice remain unknown.
Habitable zone
Estimated from incident flux and stellar temperature using the one-Earth-mass conservative boundaries from Kopparapu et al. (2014) for 2,600–7,200 K. The cooler TRAPPIST-1 system uses NASA’s published boundaries. Surface habitability depends on additional conditions.
Giant
Catalog radius of at least 6 Earth radii.
Life search
Shortlists planets in the atlas’s habitable zone with some evidence of a rocky composition. Radius-based candidates meet the rocky-candidate criteria and exceed 0.5 Earth radii. The atlas extends this size screen to 2 Earth radii for density-supported candidates with a measured mass and catalog bulk density of at least 3.5 g/cm³. The radius-based size range follows the Habitable Worlds Catalog.
Probability of life
Unknown for every exoplanet in the atlas. The evidence categories describe how each planet qualifies for follow-up. Atmosphere, surface conditions, and evidence of life require further observations. NASA’s guide to potentially habitable worlds.
Combining filters
One planet must satisfy all selected planet criteria. Search can match a host or a planet name.
Positions and orbits
The Milky Way backdrop is schematic. Catalog host positions use linear distances in galactic coordinates. The 2D orbit diagrams compress distances and use schematic orientation and phase. Dashed rings use orbit sizes estimated from orbital period and stellar mass. Orbits with no usable size appear in the planet list. Multi-star systems are represented by their catalog host point and show planets around a single diagram origin.
